Overview: Delete Member Qualification Action Plan field on the lead
Primary Entity: Lead


Generated from: C:\Automation\E2EAutomation\src\features\api\SF\SF-574.feature

## Setup Instructions:
1. Import this collection into Postman
2. Create a new environment (or use existing Salesforce QA environment)
3. Set the following environment variables:
   - `sf_client_id`: Your Connected App Consumer Key
   - `sf_client_secret`: Your Connected App Consumer Secret
   - `sf_username`: Your Salesforce username
   - `sf_password`: Your Salesforce password
   - `sf_security_token`: Your Salesforce security token
   - `sf_login_url`: Your Salesforce login URL (e.g., https://login.salesforce.com or https://test.salesforce.com)
   - `sf_api_version`: API version (e.g., v60.0)

## Authentication:
1. Run the "🔐 Get Salesforce Access Token" request first
2. The access token and instance URL will be automatically saved to collection variables
3. All subsequent requests will use this token via Bearer authentication

exec: // Save token and instance URL to collection variables
console.log("✅ Access token saved to collection variable: sf_access_token");

request.description:
Obtains a Salesforce access token using OAuth2 Username/Password flow.

**Required Environment Variables:**
- `sf_client_id`: Your Connected App Consumer Key
- `sf_client_secret`: Your Connected App Consumer Secret
- `sf_username`: Your Salesforce username
- `sf_password`: Your Salesforce password
- `sf_security_token`: Your Salesforce security token (appended to password)
- `sf_login_url`: Your Salesforce login URL (e.g., https://login.salesforce.com or https://test.salesforce.com)

**Response:**
Returns `access_token`, `instance_url`, and other OAuth details. The access token and instance URL are automatically saved to collection variables for use in subsequent requests.
